# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of remote work on engineering innovation?

Approach: OLS of patents_per_100_eng_2023 on remote_share with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and collab_index_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on remote_share is -1.950 (SE 0.226, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

input.content: {"decision":"reject","reason":"The report controls for collab_index_2023, a 2023 post-treatment variable that remote_share strongly predicts (coefficient 0.68), so it is a mediator or collider. That control creates the negative sign. My re-run without it, using only the 2020 pre-period controls, gives a positive effect of about +0.75 (SE 0.23). Without any controls the effect is about +2.3. The 'negative effect' conclusion is not supported."}

content.text:
I rejected the report and wrote `verdict.json` in the work folder. Its "negative effect" conclusion depends on a bad control.

The analyst controlled for `collab_index_2023`, a variable measured in 2023, after the remote work period. Remote share strongly predicts it (coefficient about 0.68). That makes it a mediator or collider, and controlling for it distorts the estimate.

I re-ran the regression three ways, using robust standard errors. All three used the full sample, without the analyst's 1% trim of the outcome. They differ in the controls they include:

| Controls | Coefficient on `remote_share` | SE |
|---|---|---|
| None | +2.32 | 0.24 |
| 2020 pre-period variables only | +0.75 | 0.23 |
| Pre-period variables plus `collab_index_2023` | −2.13 | 0.23 |

The third row reproduces the analyst's negative sign (their trimmed sample gives −1.95). Dropping the collaboration index makes the sign positive, so the headline result is an artifact of that one control.

I didn't test other specifications, so I can't say what the true effect is. The review only shows that the reported negative effect isn't supported.
